content.text: Los Angeles Lakers forward Lebron James (23) drives to the basket past Houston Rockets center Steven Adams, left, and Rockets' center Alperen Sengun during the second half of an NBA basketball game Thursday, Dec. 25, 2025, in Los Angeles. (AP Photo/Jayne Kamin-Oncea)APIf you purchase a product through a link on our site, we may receive compensation.By Joey Aliberti | JAliberti@syracuse.comThe Los Angeles Lakers and Houston Rockets will face off in the first round of the NBA Playoffs, with Game 1 set for Saturday at 8:30 p.m. ET. This is the first time LeBron James and Kevin Durant faced off in a non-NBA Finals series, and could be the last. Here’s what you need to know to watch every Rockets vs. Lakers playoff game. Where can I stream Rockets vs. Lakers for free?The Rockets vs. Lakers series will air on various channels and stream live on DIRECTV, which offers a free trial.Game 3 will also stream exclusively on Amazon Prime Video (free trial). Channels and streaming services are only listed for the first four games of the series, so there’s a chance of ESPN airing games later on in the series as well. NBC, ABC and ESPN will serve as the channels for all first round NBA Playoff games, with Prime Video taking exclusive rights to some games as well. DIRECTV (free trial) is the best way to watch the first round action. They have NBC, ABC and ESPN. You’ll also need a subscription to Prime Video for some of the games, which you can watch with a free trial. Rockets vs. Lakers TV ScheduleAll times in ET. ** Signifies that the game will only be played if necessary.Game 1: HOU @ LAL, Saturday, April 18, 8:30 p.m. on ABC (STREAM)Game 2: HOU @ LAL, Tuesday, April 21, 10:30 p.m. on NBC (STREAM)Game 3: LAL @ HOU, Friday, April 24, 8:00 p.m. on Prime (STREAM)Game 4: LAL @ HOU, Sunday, April 26, 9:30p.m. on NBC (STREAM)Game 5**: HOU @ LAL, Wednesday, April 29Game 6**: LAL @ HOU, Friday, May 1Game 7**: HOU @ LAL, Sunday, May 3What to know for Rockets vs. LakersThe Los Angeles Lakers could be without Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves for the entire series against Houston. That leaves 41-year-old LeBron James as the top option and only primary ball handler available for Los Angeles. The Lakers were 3-2 to end the season with Doncic and Reaves sidelined. The Rockets ended the season by winning nine of their last 10 games. This is Houston’s first playoff series with Durant around. The Rockets lost their first round series as a two-seed last season, then made a big trade to add Durant. The 37-year-old led the team in scoring, averaging 26 points per game.
